_about: Material data for seatcheck.py. SI units: E and strengths in MPa, density in kg/m3. Wood values are clear, straight-grained wood at 12% moisture content, average (mean) values after the USDA Forest Products Laboratory Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-282, 2021), Table 5-3. Tension parallel to grain is not in that table; MOR is used in its place (clear-wood tension parallel is normally higher, so this is on the safe side). Metal values are typical published figures, not guaranteed minimums unless marked. For printed metal, replace them with the print bureau's data sheet for the exact process, orientation and finish.

wood_elastic_ratios._about: Hardwood averages used to build each wood's stiffness from its E along the grain (Wood Handbook Table 5-1, rounded). The checker treats wood as transversely isotropic about the grain.

baltic birch ply._note: rough in-plane average for a crossbanded panel; treat as isotropic

316L printed LPBF._note: laser powder bed, as built. Se = fully reversed fatigue strength at about 1e7 cycles; as-built surface is rough and roughly halves it

316L printed binder jet._note: binder jet, sintered. Lower yield than LPBF; the default for 'printed stainless' when the process is unknown, since it is the weaker of the two

316L wrought._note: annealed bar/plate, ASTM A240 minimums for fy and fu

CF8M cast._note: investment-cast 316. Porosity makes fatigue scatter large

6061-T6 aluminum._note: no true endurance limit; Se is at 5e8 cycles. Welds drop to about T4 strength

brass._note: half-hard; wide range by alloy and temper

silicon bronze C87300._note: sand/investment cast, ASTM B584 typicals; fatigue value low confidence

17-4PH H1150 cast._note: cast CB7Cu-1 aged H1150, typicals; cast fatigue well below wrought, low confidence

17-4PH H900._note: peak-aged; brittle-ish (low impact toughness). Cast values run lower than these wrought typicals; low confidence

Ti-6Al-4V printed._note: laser powder bed, stress relieved + HIP. As-built surface roughly halves fatigue

maraging 1.2709 printed._note: laser powder bed, aged. Fatigue very sensitive to surface and porosity; low confidence

6061-T6 welded._note: as-welded 6061-T6 heat-affected zone (Aluminum Design Manual welded minimums, Ftyw ~105-115, Ftuw 165 MPa). Use for a whole welded frame: conservative away from the welds. Se is a rough as-welded detail value at 5e8 cycles.

6061-T6 welded tube as solid._note: For a welded 6061-T6 round tube frame (about 30 x 3 or 25.4 x 2.5) that the CAD models as solid rods: the welded-HAZ values (fy 110, fu 165, E 69000, Se 30) scaled by the tube's share of the solid rod's section modulus (about 0.58); density scaled by area (about 0.36). Bending is right; axial and shear stress come out about 1.6 x low, which is acceptable only because bending governs in tube chairs.

5052-H32 aluminum._note: SendCutSend's bendable aluminium sheet. ASM / Aluminum Association typical values; Se is the R.R. Moore value at 5e8 cycles. Bends keep about H32 strength.

GFRC premix._note: Brittle cast composite, premix (poured, vibrated, AR glass fibre about 3%), 28-day. fy here is the flexural limit of proportionality (LOP, first crack, about 6-8 MPa per PCI MNL-130 / GRCA for premix), fu the modulus of rupture (about 10-14 MPa premix; sprayed GFRC is about 20-30). The checker's von Mises vs fy is conservative in tension and very conservative in compression (compressive strength is about 40-60 MPa); a pass means no first crack at the safety factor. Se is about 55% of LOP for 1e7 cycles. Lives under 'metal' only so the isotropic checks apply. Replace with the caster's test data.

pad._about: Cushions, leather, upholstery: no stiffness in the model, they pass the load down to whatever they sit on. Density in kg/m3 for weight and tipping.

bolts._about: Tensile stress area As in mm2. fy = 0.2% proof stress, fu = tensile strength, MPa (ISO 3506 for stainless, ISO 898-1 / SAE J429 for carbon steel).

wood_screws._about: Withdrawal from side grain, NDS 12.2: wood screw W = 2850 G^2 D lb per inch of thread in the main member (reference design value, already has a safety factor of about 5 on the average ultimate). Lag screw W = 1800 G^1.5 D^0.75. End grain: 75% of those for lag screws; wood screws are not rated in end grain (treat as zero).
